intent.goal: Register a supplier purchase exactly once and reflect it in inventory and finance.
invariants: A purchase_id may affect stock at most once.
A settled Action replay must be observationally idempotent.
Financial and stock projections must refer to the same purchase_id.

actions.description: Resolve purchased product identities and quantities.
Apply resolved purchase quantities to stock.
postconditions: stock reflects the purchase exactly once

actions.description: Record the financial expense for the purchase.

logs: retry resumed flow from action boundary preceding unsettled expense
observable_input.error: Intent settlement rejected: stock projection diverged from purchase quantity; expected +12, observed +24.

gold_codemanager.thesis: IncreaseStock is not idempotent under replay of the same purchase_id, so recovery after a downstream failure reapplies the stock mutation.
gold_codemanager.mechanism: The trace shows the same purchase_id entering IncreaseStock twice around a downstream RecordPurchaseExpense retry, and the observed stock delta is exactly doubled while the financial expense is recorded once.
causal_chain: RecordPurchaseExpense times out after IncreaseStock already succeeded.
Recovery re-enters IncreaseStock for the same purchase_id.
IncreaseStock does not recognize the prior applied effect.
The same quantity is applied twice.
Settlement detects stock/finance divergence.
falsification_criteria: If replaying the same purchase_id twice does not duplicate stock with the current implementation, reject this thesis.
If evidence shows the two IncreaseStock calls used different purchase identities, reject this thesis.
alternative_causes: checkpoint incorrectly resumed before the last proven Action
gold_codemanager.solution_request: Modify only Commerce.IncreaseStock/implementation.zig. Make application of a stock increase idempotent for the same purchase_id while preserving the existing contract. Explain how the implementation prevents the observed replay from producing a second stock effect, and state which invariants hidden integration tests should verify.

gold_solution.causal_explanation: The failure is caused by replay, not by the quantity itself: a downstream timeout causes the flow to invoke IncreaseStock again with the same purchase_id. Because the implementation performs the mutation without an idempotency decision tied to that purchase identity, both invocations realize an effect.
gold_solution.proposed_change: Change IncreaseStock so it deterministically recognizes whether the effect for the current purchase_id has already been committed and returns the same semantic success without applying the stock delta again. Keep the decision and mutation atomic from the Action's perspective.
gold_solution.predicted_effect: On replay of purchase_id=P-884, the second invocation produces no additional stock delta, so stock remains +12 while the downstream expense retry can complete.
risks: non-atomic check-then-write could still duplicate under concurrency
idempotency key must not collapse distinct purchases
verification: same purchase_id replay produces one stock effect
different purchase_ids with equal payloads each produce their own effect
concurrent duplicate invocations preserve exactly-once semantic effect

intent.goal: Close a sale with inventory and financial totals consistent with the accepted line items.
invariants: sum(line totals) equals sale total under the declared money rounding rule
stock quantities are unaffected by monetary normalization

actions.description: Decrease stock for resolved sold quantities.
postconditions: inventory decreased exactly by sold quantities
sale total equals normalized sum of line totals

traces: close-sale normalize line totals before aggregate=false
observable_input.error: Money invariant violation: finalized total differs from declared normalized total by 0.01.

gold_codemanager.thesis: CloseSale aggregates unnormalized decimal line values and rounds only after summation, while the contract expects line-level monetary normalization before aggregation.
gold_codemanager.mechanism: The stock path is correct and the trace explicitly shows aggregate-before-normalize; the one-cent discrepancy is characteristic of applying the rounding boundary at the wrong stage.
causal_chain: Three line values contain fractional currency precision.
CloseSale sums raw decimals.
The aggregate is rounded once at the end.
The contract's line-level normalization produces a different cent result.
Settlement rejects the financial total.
falsification_criteria: If line-level normalization followed by aggregation still yields 19.99, reject this thesis.
If the declared contract specifies aggregate-level rounding, reject this thesis.
alternative_causes: binary floating representation without fixed-point semantics
gold_codemanager.solution_request: Modify only Commerce.CloseSale/implementation.zig. Align monetary aggregation with the declared normalization boundary without changing schemas or tests. Explain why the change removes the 0.01 drift and how it preserves totals for already-normalized values.

gold_solution.causal_explanation: The causal defect is the order of operations. Raw values with more precision than the currency scale are aggregated first, so the final rounding is not equivalent to the contract's per-line monetary normalization.
gold_solution.proposed_change: Normalize each monetary line to the canonical currency representation before summing, then aggregate using the exact money type already required by the Action contract.
gold_solution.predicted_effect: The computed total follows the same normalization semantics as the accepted lines and matches 20.00 for this execution.
risks: changing rounding mode instead of only rounding location would alter semantics
using floating point internally could preserve nondeterministic edge cases
verification: fractional-cent lines match contract total
already-normalized lines are unchanged
negative/discount lines preserve the same rounding law

intent.goal: Update a product price and immediately expose the accepted value to the current execution.
invariants: the Intent response must not claim a price older than the acknowledged write
event identity and returned entity_id must match

actions.description: Read current product projection for response.
postconditions: returned product is at least the required version for this Intent

logs: read-product accepted cache hit without version fence
observable_input.error: Read-your-write invariant violated: required version 42, returned version 41.

gold_codemanager.thesis: ReadProduct accepts a cache hit without enforcing the minimum required version carried by the Intent, allowing a stale projection to satisfy the read immediately after a write.
gold_codemanager.mechanism: The write is acknowledged at version 42, the read declares required_version=42, but the Action returns cache version 41 in 4ms while projection lag is nonzero.
causal_chain: UpdatePrice commits version 42.
The cache still contains version 41.
ReadProduct checks presence but not freshness against required_version.
It returns the stale value.
The Intent-level read-your-write invariant fails.
falsification_criteria: If ReadProduct already rejects cache entries below required_version, reject this thesis.
If version 42 was not committed before the read started, reject this thesis.
gold_codemanager.solution_request: Modify only Commerce.ReadProduct/implementation.zig. Preserve cache use when valid, but make the Action respect the required version supplied by the execution. Explain the causal link between the stale cache acceptance and the proposed freshness decision.

gold_solution.causal_explanation: The cache is not inherently wrong; the defect is treating any cache hit as authoritative when the caller requires a minimum committed version. That turns normal projection lag into an Intent-visible stale read.
gold_solution.proposed_change: Gate cache acceptance on cached_version >= required_version. When the cache is older, use the Action's existing authoritative/fallback read path rather than returning the stale value.
gold_solution.predicted_effect: Version 41 will no longer satisfy a read requiring 42, while cache hits at 42 or newer remain fast.
risks: fallback path could increase latency under projection lag

intent.goal: Confirm a payment once and trigger exactly one downstream fulfillment transition.
invariants: one payment confirmation produces at most one PaymentConfirmed event
retries may repeat computation but not external semantic effects

actions.description: Verify provider evidence for a payment.
Persist confirmation and emit semantic confirmation event.
postconditions: one confirmation effect and one event

traces: confirm-payment publish attempt=1 timeout awaiting ack
broker observed duplicate semantic event id differs
logs: publish retry created new event_id instead of replaying stable event identity
observable_input.error: Downstream fulfillment rejected duplicate state transition for the same payment.

gold_codemanager.thesis: ConfirmPayment regenerates event identity on publish retry, turning one persisted confirmation into two distinct semantic PaymentConfirmed events.
gold_codemanager.mechanism: Persistence commits once, but a lost/late publish acknowledgement triggers a retry. Because the second publication receives a new event identity, downstream deduplication cannot recognize it as the same effect.
causal_chain: Payment confirmation is persisted once.
First event publication succeeds but acknowledgement is not observed.
Retry path constructs a fresh event identity.
Broker/downstream sees two different events for the same confirmation.
Fulfillment executes twice and rejects the second transition.
falsification_criteria: If both observed PaymentConfirmed events share the same stable event identity, reject this thesis.
If two distinct payment confirmations were committed, reject this thesis.
alternative_causes: broker duplicated a single event identity
gold_codemanager.solution_request: Modify only Commerce.ConfirmPayment/implementation.zig. Ensure retry of event publication represents the same semantic effect rather than creating a new one. Explain how stable identity ties the retry to the original committed confirmation.

gold_solution.causal_explanation: The downstream duplicate exists because the retry is semantically indistinguishable from a second confirmation: it has a new event identity. The retry must replay the same effect identity generated for the committed confirmation.
gold_solution.proposed_change: Derive or persist the confirmation event identity once before publication and reuse it across publish retries for that confirmation execution.
gold_solution.predicted_effect: A lost acknowledgement may cause transport-level redelivery, but all deliveries carry the same semantic event identity and collapse to one fulfillment effect.
risks: event identity must remain unique across genuinely different confirmations
verification: publish retry reuses event identity
separate payments use separate identities
restart between commit and publish preserves the original event identity

intent.goal: Move quantity between two stock locations atomically.
invariants: total quantity across source and destination is conserved
concurrent transfers must terminate without deadlock

actions.description: Atomically decrement source and increment destination.

observable_input.error: Both stock transfer executions exceeded lock deadline without progress.

gold_codemanager.thesis: ApplyStockTransfer acquires source then destination locks according to transfer direction, allowing opposite-direction transfers to acquire the same pair in reverse order and deadlock.
gold_codemanager.mechanism: The trace is a complete circular wait: T1 holds A and waits B while T2 holds B and waits A, with low CPU and IO indicating waiting rather than resource saturation.
causal_chain: T1 locks source A.
T2 locks source B.
T1 requests destination B held by T2.
T2 requests destination A held by T1.
Neither can progress before timeout.
falsification_criteria: If the implementation already acquires location locks in a global deterministic order, reject this thesis.
If one trace did not actually hold its first lock while waiting for the second, reject this thesis.
alternative_causes: external long transaction holding both locations
gold_codemanager.solution_request: Modify only Commerce.ApplyStockTransfer/implementation.zig. Preserve atomic transfer semantics while preventing opposite-direction lock inversion. Explain the ordering rule and why it breaks the observed circular wait.

gold_solution.causal_explanation: Deadlock arises from direction-dependent lock ordering. Two executions need the same lock set but acquire it in opposite sequences, satisfying the circular-wait condition.
gold_solution.proposed_change: Determine a canonical ordering for the two location lock keys independent of transfer direction, acquire them in that order, then apply source/destination semantics after both locks are held.
gold_solution.predicted_effect: A->B and B->A contend on the same first lock instead of each holding one lock and waiting on the other, eliminating this circular deadlock class.
risks: canonical ordering must be total and stable
partial acquisition failure must release already-held locks
verification: opposite-direction concurrent transfers terminate
same-direction contention remains correct
quantity conservation holds under high concurrency

intent.goal: Import a supplier invoice even when optional provider metadata is absent.
invariants: optional external metadata must not become a required domain fact
canonical invoice totals must remain unchanged

actions.description: Parse provider payload into canonical invoice fields.
postconditions: required fields canonical; optional fields may be absent

observable_input.error: ParseSupplierInvoice aborted: attempted unwrap of null optional field driver_count.

gold_codemanager.thesis: The parser implementation treats optional driver_count as mandatory by unwrapping it, contradicting the Action contract that allows absence.
gold_codemanager.mechanism: All required fields are present; the trace terminates exactly at an optional field unwrap, so the failure is local to representation handling rather than domain validation.
causal_chain: Provider omits an optional field.
Parser reads null.
Implementation force-unwraps the optional value.
Action aborts before producing the canonical invoice.
The Intent fails despite all required facts being available.
falsification_criteria: If driver_count is required by the current Action contract, reject this thesis.
If the panic occurs before driver_count access, reject this thesis.
alternative_causes: schema/version mismatch between runtime and parser
gold_codemanager.solution_request: Modify only Commerce.ParseSupplierInvoice/implementation.zig. Respect the declared optionality of driver_count without inventing a domain value. Explain how absence propagates safely while required-field failures remain errors.

gold_solution.causal_explanation: The implementation introduces a stronger precondition than the contract by requiring an optional provider field. That converts a valid input into a runtime failure.
gold_solution.proposed_change: Handle the optional value explicitly and preserve absence in the canonical representation (or omit the optional projection) instead of force-unwrapping it. Keep required fields unchanged.
gold_solution.predicted_effect: Payloads missing driver_count parse successfully while malformed required data still fails through existing validation.
risks: defaulting to zero would falsely assert a domain fact

intent.goal: Return every transaction exactly once across cursor-paginated pages.
invariants: no committed transaction may be skipped
no transaction may appear twice when following returned cursors

actions.description: Read one stable ordered page and return next cursor.
postconditions: page is strictly ordered and cursor resumes after final item

observable_input.error: Pagination completeness invariant failed: T051 absent from concatenated pages.

gold_codemanager.thesis: The cursor encodes only timestamp while the declared stable order is the composite (timestamp,id), so rows sharing the boundary timestamp can be skipped.
gold_codemanager.mechanism: Page 1 ends at (1000,T050); T051 has the same timestamp but a higher id. A page-2 predicate of timestamp>1000 excludes it even though it comes after the boundary in the declared order.
causal_chain: Results are ordered by timestamp then id.
Cursor loses the id component.
Resume predicate advances past the whole timestamp bucket.
T051 is excluded from all subsequent pages.
Completeness invariant fails.
falsification_criteria: If the cursor already carries both timestamp and id, reject this thesis.
If stable ordering is timestamp-only and timestamps are guaranteed unique, reject this thesis.
alternative_causes: transaction inserted between pages without snapshot semantics
gold_codemanager.solution_request: Modify only Commerce.ReadTransactionPage/implementation.zig. Make cursor generation/resume consistent with the declared composite order. Explain how the cursor represents the exact boundary and prevents both skipping and duplication.

gold_solution.causal_explanation: Pagination is incorrect because the resume key is less expressive than the sort key. The implementation cannot distinguish records that share the page boundary timestamp.
gold_solution.proposed_change: Encode the complete ordered key (timestamp,id) in the cursor and resume with the lexicographic predicate strictly after that composite key.
gold_solution.predicted_effect: T051 is included on page 2 while T050 is not repeated, preserving exact traversal of equal-timestamp records.
risks: cursor encoding must be deterministic and backward handling explicit
comparison must use the exact same ordering semantics as the query
verification: equal-timestamp boundary does not skip rows
no duplicate boundary row
multi-page traversal returns every row exactly once
